children: Framework contemplates potential non-equity funding of up to $55.5 million, which could include the right to acquire up to 50% of potential future tungsten production, subject to definitive agreements and applicable approvals as noted below
BOISE, Idaho, Nov. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Perpetua Resources Corp. (Nasdaq: PPTA) (

) ("Perpetua" or the "Company") today announced that Perpetua and its subsidiary, Perpetua Resources Idaho, Inc., have entered into a non-binding memorandum of understanding ("MOU") with a major aerospace and defense company to evaluate potential funding and future supply arrangements supporting a domestic tungsten supply chain.

The possible engagement under Perpetua's Industrial Tungsten Acceleration Program ("I-TAP") considers potential non-equity funding of up to $55.5 million at the potential funding party's sole discretion and a right for that party to acquire up to 50% of Perpetua's potential future tungsten production.

"Stibnite offers an opportunity to evaluate a potential American source of tungsten," said Jon Cherry, President and CEO of Perpetua Resources. "This MOU allows us to explore how early engagement with the U.S. manufacturing industry could support our work to assess the material, processing options, and potential development pathways."

The MOU does not commit either party to provide funding, to purchase or sell tungsten, or to grant supply rights. Any binding funding or supply arrangements would require definitive written agreements, satisfactory due diligence, applicable approvals, and satisfaction of other conditions. There can be no assurance that definitive agreements will be executed.

Tungsten is used in defense systems and advanced manufacturing, and there are no sources currently mined in the United States. Perpetua is currently evaluating whether mineralization in the historic Stibnite Mining District and related claims in Idaho could support a commercially viable domestic source.

Any future tungsten development would be separate from Perpetua's approved gold-antimony mine plan for the Stibnite Gold Project and would require additional environmental review and permitting. Evaluation activities do not assure commercial viability or future production.

The contemplated I-TAP would advance the Company's previously announced tungsten evaluation program. If agreed to and funded, initial work is expected to include exploration drilling, resource definition, metallurgical and processing testing, and decline design and permitting. A potential second phase could include underground exploration and development, preliminary economic evaluation, pilot-scale processing, and assessment of recovery circuits.
J.P. Morgan acted as financial advisor to Perpetua Resources Corp. in connection with the investment contemplated by the MOU.

Perpetua Resources Corp., through its wholly owned subsidiaries, is focused on the exploration, site restoration, and redevelopment of gold-antimony-tungsten deposits in the Stibnite-Yellow Pine district of central Idaho. The Stibnite Gold Project is one of the highest-grade, open-pit gold deposits in the United States and holds the only identified domestic reserve of the critical mineral antimony, which is essential to the defense, energy, and manufacturing sectors. The Project is designed to apply a modern, responsible mining approach to restore a historic mine site and provide uplift to water quality, improve fish habitat access, and invest in river restoration while supporting local economic development in rural Idaho.
